methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Lab 91 is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Stage-progression anchoring is the applicable method here. Using the $10M total raised as a proxy for entry valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to next-stage financing yields $25M. This implies a low-to-high range of $21M to $29M, with $25M as the median. The peer-median approach could not be applied: while 12 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, similar valuation tier) yielded fewer than 3 comparable datapoints, making sector-wide medians unreliable. Public-comp anchoring using the 3-ticker Semiconductors P/S median of 21.4x is not feasible without the target's revenue, which private companies rarely disclose.

The analysis supports a $21M–$29M valuation band, centered at $25M. Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow-set peer pricing, absence of revenue data to validate public-market multiples, and limited precision in using total raised as a valuation proxy at seed stage. Tightening this range would require either comparable transaction data from peer seed rounds or disclosure of Lab 91's revenue trajectory.
